14.1.title: Demo-path determinism
14.1.summary: All 7 demo steps are timer-driven with pre-cached JSON data. No external API calls, no blockchain confirmations, no random values, no mutable external state. Determinism is excellent. Minor risk: timer-based phase transitions are hardcoded and do not adapt to presenter pacing.

steps.name: Landing Page (0:00-0:10)
steps.mechanism: Pure React render. Static hero text, integration strip, TEE badge all hardcoded in page.tsx:52-110.
failure_modes: Browser fails to load fonts (Press Start 2P + Space Mono via next/font)

steps.name: LOAD DEMO (0:10-0:20)
steps.mechanism: launchDemo() injects hardcoded addresses ['0xDemo...', 'SolDemo...'] then calls handleAnalyze. Defined at page.tsx:13-14.
failure_modes: Button click not registered (mitigated by Playwright stress test #11, #14-15)

steps.name: ANALYZE + Scanning (0:20-0:30)
steps.mechanism: POST /api/analyze → DEMO_MODE or cacheExists() → loadAllDemoData() reads 9 static JSON files from src/data/cache/. All data pre-computed. No network calls.
failure_modes: Cache file missing (mitigated: throws clear error 'Run scripts/seed-demo.ts first' per cache.ts:10-12)
fs.readFileSync fails on read-only filesystem (Vercel serverless supports fs reads of bundled files)

steps.name: Results (0:30-0:45)
steps.mechanism: setTimeout(() => setPhase('results'), 2000) in page.tsx:22. Auto-advances 2s after analyze completes. Results rendered from pre-cached API response.
failure_modes: Timer drift on underpowered machine (unlikely; 2s is generous)
API response >2s (stress test shows 50-70ms per STRESS-TEST-REPORT.md Phase 7)

steps.name: Roast Battle (0:45-0:65)
steps.mechanism: setTimeout(..., 20000) triggers GET /api/roast → loadRoastBattle() reads roast-battle.json or roast-lines.json + personas.json from cache. Auto-advances at T+20s. Graceful fallback: .catch(() => setPhase('battle')) — advances even on fetch failure.
failure_modes: Roast API failure (mitigated: catch advances phase anyway)
5-round battle renders differently on different viewports (stress test #20 passed at both 320px and 1440px)

steps.name: Compare Card (0:65-0:75)
steps.mechanism: setTimeout(..., 58000) triggers GET /api/compare → loadComparison() reads comparison.json from cache. Auto-advances at T+58s. Graceful fallback: .catch(() => setPhase('compare')).
failure_modes: Compare API failure (mitigated: catch advances phase anyway)
Negative percentage rendering (stress test #23 verified: no double sign on -8.3%)

steps.name: CTA (0:75-0:90)
steps.mechanism: setTimeout(() => setPhase('cta'), 76000) in page.tsx:26. Auto-advances at T+76s. Static content: ATTESTATION VERIFIED badge, PaymentButton tier='Snapshot', OKX.AI footer.
failure_modes: Payment button simulation may confuse judges (footgun #2, mitigated by presenter script)

determinism_enhancers: All 9 cache files are static JSON in src/data/cache/ — no external API calls in demo path
DEMO_MODE env var or cacheExists() gates the pre-cached path in analyze/route.ts:10
All phase timers are set simultaneously in handleAnalyze (page.tsx:22-26), ensuring consistent relative timing
launchDemo() uses hardcoded demo addresses — no user input variability
Stress test verified 33/33 Playwright browser tests passing end-to-end

determinism_risks.risk: Timer-based phases are rigid — if presenter lingers on results, battle auto-starts at T+20s regardless
determinism_risks.mitigation: Presenter must follow DEMO-SCRIPT.md pacing. Could add pause/resume controls for live demo flexibility.

determinism_risks.risk: All 4 timers share one phaseTimers ref; if handleAnalyze is called again, old timers are cleared but new ones start from scratch
determinism_risks.mitigation: useEffect cleanup clears timers on unmount. Double-click prevention tested (stress test #15).

14.2.title: Failure fallback
14.2.summary: All 4 footguns have documented workarounds. Code-level fallbacks are robust: API failures gracefully advance phases instead of crashing. Social mitigations for footguns 1 (TEE mock) and 2 (x402 mock) are adequate for hackathon but would not survive deep technical scrutiny. The 'don't linger' strategy for the TEE mock is the weakest link.

footguns.title: TEE attestation is pre-computed mock
footguns.planned_mitigation: Don't linger on attestation text. Mention 'TEE-sealed' verbally, move on.
footguns.assessment: The attestation text 'ATTESTATION: 0x7f3a...b91e' is hardcoded in page.tsx:109 (landing footer) and page.tsx:160 (CTA phase). It never changes. A judge who inspects the page source will see it's static. The verbal mitigation ('mention TEE-sealed, move on') is thin. No code-level fallback exists — this is purely presenter-dependent.
footguns.improvement: Could add a small animation or loading state on the attestation badge to create illusion of verification in progress.

footguns.title: x402 payment is simulated
footguns.planned_mitigation: Click past quickly. Frame as 'payment gate integration proof.'
footguns.assessment: PaymentButton component (imported in page.tsx:9) renders a 'Simulate Payment' flow. The 3-state transition (idle → simulating → done) gives visual plausibility. The verbal framing as 'integration proof' is honest enough for a hackathon demo.
footguns.improvement: Label change from 'Simulate Payment' to 'Payment Gate (x402)' would reduce judge suspicion.

footguns.title: Data is pre-cached
footguns.planned_mitigation: Only use LOAD DEMO. Never type random addresses.
footguns.assessment: Strong: the LOAD DEMO button is visually prominent. Real addresses typed manually would hit the live code path which calls OnchainOS API (requires API keys that may not be configured in demo env). The 'Demo Mode — Pre-computed Data' badge (page.tsx:69-72) is visible to the audience. This is transparent and well-managed.

footguns.title: OnchainOS not live
footguns.planned_mitigation: Frame as 'demo mode with pre-loaded wallets.'
footguns.assessment: The scanning phase says 'Connecting to OnchainOS...' (page.tsx:115) which is technically misleading since it reads from cache. But the demo mode badge and presenter framing compensate. Overall acceptable for hackathon.

code_level_fallbacks.triggers_on: POST /api/analyze network failure, JSON parse failure
code_level_fallbacks.behavior: Returns to landing page — user can retry
Advances to battle phase anyway (battleData will be null, RoastBattle may render empty)
code_level_fallbacks.adequacy: PARTIAL — battle may render blank if data fetch fails

code_level_fallbacks.behavior: Advances to compare phase anyway (compareData will be null)
code_level_fallbacks.adequacy: PARTIAL — compare card may render blank

code_level_fallbacks.mechanism: Throws descriptive error if cache file missing

14.3.title: Demo-state isolation
14.3.summary: The demo deployment on Vercel is self-contained with no shared mutable state. All data is static JSON files bundled with the deployment. The Vercel OIDC token reveals the deployment is in the 'development' environment, not 'production'. The demo URL https://alter-ego.vercel.app maps to the production domain, but the token shows development env — suggesting the production deployment may be on a different environment or the token is stale. No shared database, no cross-deployment state leakage.

vercel_environment.note: The demo URL alter-ego.vercel.app is the production domain, but the OIDC token is for development env. This may indicate the token is from a preview deployment or the production env uses a different token.

evidence.state_mechanism: All state is file-based: 9 static JSON files in src/data/cache/. No database, no Redis, no external state store.
evidence.api_routes: All 4 API routes (analyze, roast, compare, persona) read from local filesystem only. No cross-origin requests in demo path.
shared_state_risks: If the same Vercel deployment is used for both dev testing and live demo, manual cache mutations during dev could affect the demo. Mitigation: cache files are read-only at runtime (no write endpoints exist).

The Vercel preview URL (alter-e8wzy3vsl-damilolas-projects-fafdf859.vercel.app from VIDEO-PLAN.md) is a separate deployment from the production URL (alter-ego.vercel.app from DEMO-SCRIPT.md). These are isolated.

14.3.isolation_score: STRONG — static data, no shared state, separate preview/production deployments

14.4.title: Screen-recording backup
14.4.summary: Pre-recorded backup video exists at video/demo-final.mp4. Directory listing confirms the file is present alongside VIDEO-PLAN.md which documents the recording process. DEMO-SCRIPT.md claims 86s duration.

evidence.verification_method: list_dir returned the file in listing
evidence.note: VIDEO-PLAN.md references a different URL (alter-e8wzy3vsl-damilolas-projects-fafdf859.vercel.app) than DEMO-SCRIPT.md (alter-ego.vercel.app). The backup may have been recorded against a preview deployment, not the production URL.

risks: The backup video URL (preview deployment) differs from the live demo URL (production). If the production deployment differs significantly, the backup won't match the live experience.
Could not verify the MP4 file is playable and complete (binary file, 86s as claimed). File exists on disk but content not validated.

14.5.title: Environment readiness
14.5.summary: The demo is a standard Next.js app served via Vercel. No special browser requirements: no MetaMask, no Chrome-only APIs, no wallet extensions needed. Playwright was used for stress testing but the demo itself uses standard web APIs. Any modern browser (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge) at 1280×800 should work. Fonts loaded via next/font (self-hosted, no external CDN dependency).

requirements.browser: Any modern browser (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge)
requirements.extensions: None required. DevTools should be closed (cosmetic only).
requirements.wallet: No MetaMask or wallet extension needed. Demo uses pre-cached data with no wallet connection.
requirements.network: Internet required to load Vercel deployment. No blockchain RPC calls in demo path.
requirements.fonts: Press Start 2P + Space Mono loaded via next/font (self-hosted, no Google Fonts CDN dependency)
requirements.special: CRT scanline/flicker/vignette CSS effects — GPU-accelerated, works in all modern browsers

14.5.stress_test_verification: STRESS-TEST-REPORT.md confirms 33/33 Playwright tests passing in Chromium at both 320px and 1440px viewports. Slow 3G test passed at 21.8s.

potential_issues.issue: Firefox/Safari may render CRT effects slightly differently (CSS filter compatibility)
potential_issues.mitigation: CRT effects use standard CSS (backdrop-filter, clip-path). Stress tests only ran in Chromium (Playwright). Presenter should use Chrome for best fidelity.

potential_issues.issue: Fonts may take 1-2s to load on first visit, causing layout shift
potential_issues.mitigation: DEMO-SCRIPT.md explicitly says 'pre-load page before recording'. Presenter should open the URL before going on stage.

recommendations: CRITICAL: Verify the production deployment (alter-ego.vercel.app) is up and matches the preview deployment used for the backup video. Discrepancy could cause visual differences.
HIGH: Pre-load the demo page 30s before stage time to warm fonts and avoid FOUT (Flash of Unstyled Text).
MEDIUM: Consider adding a pause button or phase indicator so presenter can adapt pacing without fighting auto-advancing timers.
MEDIUM: The TEE attestation mock is the weakest demo element. If questioned by judges, have a prepared response about TEE infrastructure being post-hackathon.
LOW: Use Chrome for the live demo (CRT effects tested in Chromium only).
LOW: Verify demo-final.mp4 is playable end-to-end before stage. The file exists but content was not validated.
